text:
incident-bot: PAGING: control-plane 5xx spike (>8% P95) detected across auth/org-lookup/billing backends in us-west. Error mix: 502 from auth-proxy, 504 org-lookup timeouts, intermittent 500s from billing. First seen: 2026-03-15T06:12:25Z. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ctlplane/ctlplane-5xx?from=now-15m
Maya (oncall): Ack. I'm oncall for this window, joining. @Jordan can you grab logs for auth-proxy?
Jordan: digging in. Auth proxy logs show a sudden jump in upstream 502s around 06:11: log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T06:11:07Z auth-proxy ERROR upstream_response 502 token-service connection refused
2026-03-15T06:11:14Z auth-proxy ERROR upstream_response 502 token-service connection refused
```
Jordan: Looks like token-service instances in us-west hit connection refused & retries causing head-of-line; org-lookup calls start timing out because auth tokens can't be fetched.
Lee: Noticed redis-cache miss rate jumped at same time on org-lookup path, which increases downstream pressure. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/cache/cache-metrics?var-region=us-west
Samir: This smells like a small-scale cascade: token-service errors -> auth-proxy 502 -> clients retry -> org-lookup timeouts. We should open circuit on org-lookup and enable fallback-to-local-cache for reads.
Maya (oncall): Agreed. Runbook says: 1) identify offending service 2) open circuit breakers 3) apply local cache fallback 4) mitigate traffic (rate-limit) 5) pager handoff once stable. Running runbook: `/runbook controlplane-dep-cascade` 
ops-bot: Runbook started by Maya (oncall). Step 1: Triage. Step 2: Notify oncall SRE.
Caroline (PM): Customer impact check: Are user-facing auth flows failing or just control-plane telemetry? Any 5xx affecting hosted API tokens?
Jordan: We're seeing a 12% increase in client-facing token-exchange failures for hosted API (us-west). That means some customer requests fail with 401/502 depending on client. I recommend a status page update: partial degradation for auth-dependent features in us-west.
Maya (oncall): Action items: 1) Jordan - scale token-service pool + restart failing pods; 2) Lee - flip org-lookup circuit breaker to OPEN for 30s -> 3) Samir - enable local cache fallback for org-lookup queries; 4) ops-bot - apply rate limit headroom on auth-proxy (throttle non-critical paths). I'm taking incident lead.
Jordan: Scaling token-service now: `kubectl scale deploy/token-service -n controlplane --replicas=6`; watching pods: `CrashLoopBackOff` on one container image variant. Investigating container logs from 06:09-06:13.
Lee: Circuit breaker toggle: `POST /admin/circuit/org-lookup?action=open&duration=30s` -> response 200. Circuit open. Starting fallback to local cache for read-only endpoints.
Samir: Flipping fallback: `configctl set controlplane.orglookup.fallback local-cache true --env=us-west` -> confirmed. Local cache hit-rate increased to 78% within 90s.
ops-bot: Rate limit insertion: auth-proxy-route `customer-requests` set to 1500 rps from 5000 rps. Command executed by ops-bot.
Jordan: Token-service pods coming up but heavy GC in logs; one instance stuck in startup loop referencing KMS timeouts to vault. Possibly a transient KMS latency spike impacting token-service startup auth to KMS.
Ryan (SRE): Noted spike in KMS latency in us-west 06:09-06:14. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/kms/kms-latency?from=now-30m. If KMS calls are failing, token-service can't decrypt keys and errors out. We should escalate to infra-kms oncall.
Maya (oncall): Paging infra-kms: @infra-kms-oncall — KMS latency spike affecting token-service startup in us-west, causing cascade. Can infra-kms confirm degradations?
Jordan: For immediate mitigation, I've pushed a temporary config to token-service to use cached decrypted keys (if available) and to skip KMS refresh for 10m: `TOKEN_SERVICE_USE_CACHED_KEYS=true` -> rollout 06:21 (canary in us-west).
Lee: Observing auth 502s drop to 3% after circuit open and cached-keys flag. Org-lookup 504s down to baseline. Billing 500s remain but tracking to the same dependency chain (auth checks failing before billing writes).
Caroline (PM): Comms proposal: status.redwood.com note: "Partial degradation in us-west impacting token exchanges and auth-dependent features. Mitigation in progress; estimated recovery 30-45 minutes. Incident lead: Maya (oncall)." Agree? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Maya (oncall): Agree. Please post. @Caroline can you coordinate external comms?
Caroline (PM): I'll draft and post in 5. Also notify top-10 enterprise contacts via Ops Slack channel.
Samir: I've created a short-lived fallback policy to route sensitive auth checks to controlplane-dedicated nodes with higher retries disabled to avoid amplifying load: `trafficctl route set --path /auth/exchange --target dedicated-pool --retries=0`
ops-bot: Route change executed. Traffic to /auth/exchange now goes to dedicated-pool.
Jordan: Rolling restart of token-service stable image replacing failing variant. New pods healthy at 06:32. Token-service errors trend down.
Maya (oncall): Re-evaluating impact: 5xx rate now 1.2% (baseline 0.8%). Customer-facing errors greatly reduced. Continue monitoring 30m, then perform handoff if stable.
Ryan (SRE): I'll take over monitoring for the next 30m and prepare runbook actions for post-incident: list suspects (KMS latency, image regression, cache warmup), and start collect logs for postmortem.
Caroline (PM): Draft posted to status.redwood.com and Ops messages sent to top contacts. No customer escalations yet but one partner reported token errors at 06:16 — monitoring their case.
Maya (oncall): Handoff incoming in 15 minutes to Ryan (SRE). If anyone else needs to join post-incident RCA, please DM Samir.
Jordan: Noting a follow-up: image variant had a subtle dependency bump that intensified KMS client backoff behavior. Will open PR to revert until proper backoff smoothing and metrics are added.
Samir: Assigning postmortem owner: Samir. Target: triage doc + timeline within 24h, full RCA in 72h.
Maya (oncall): Final: incident status -> mitigated, monitoring. Handoff to Ryan at 06:40 UTC. Thanks all. :tada:
Ryan (SRE): Taking over. I'll keep thread updated with any regression.
incident-bot: Incident: control-plane dependency cascade - mitigated. Severity: Sev2 -> monitoring. Incident ID: INC-20260315-001. Pager cleared at 06:40:20Z.
